title: Why the same natural mind brings forth fruit sweet in one place and bitter in another
reading:
Look at what happens within you when a new perception is being formed. The Lord shapes it through the five degrees of the natural mind, and the same five degrees through which it is shaped can also be the means by which it is undone. The warmth of love and the cooling of true thought together nourish what is rising in you, so that the whole tree of perception comes into its proper growth, root to fruit; this is how a new bud, when it is the Lord's, is brought into being and adorned in the natural.

But the natural mind is not in one condition everywhere within you. Place by place a lack and a diminishment enter, and an affliction settles upon what was meant to grow sweet. Where the proprium is operative — the disordered natural that the soul has claimed and not yet laid off — it floods the very same elements with its own shadow. The faculties through which the Lord was nourishing the bud become the faculties through which the proprium presses its claim, and the fruit that issues there is bitter; men stumble in themselves and lose the right use of their minds because of this energy working in what they have not recognized as not their own.

So one ground bears sweetness and another bitterness, not because the natural mind is two different things, but because in one part of you the bud is being formed under the Lord's ordering and in another the same forming is being inundated by what the soul has appropriated. The fruits perish on every tree the shadow reaches. The remedy is not in the elements; it is in recognition — in discriminating, where the bitterness comes, what has been claimed, and laying it off, so that the same five degrees through which the proprium was destroying the bud can again be the degrees through which the Lord is nourishing it.
